newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel says has made safety changes.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel says has made safety changes.

text.p: Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel said on Tuesday it had already implemented most of the recommendations made by a safety authority regarding last year's tunnel fire.

A Eurotunnel spokeswoman said the company viewed the report by the Channel Tunnel Safety Authority as a "good indication" that the company would get the go-ahead to restart its freight services, which were shut down after last November's fire.
She added that a final decision on Eurotunnel's Heavy Goods Vehicles (HGV) services could come as early as Tuesday or Wednesday.
The Anglo-French Intergovernmental Commission is the body that will make the final decision following the safety authority's report early on Tuesday.
"The report is a good indication that the IGC may give the go-ahead," said Eurotunnel spokeswoman Anne Leva. However, she added that she could not pre-empt what the IGC would decide.

"The next step, really, is to wait for the go-ahead from the IGC. And assuming that we receive that, we would then restart a trial with a view to bringing the service back into full service perhaps by mid-June," she said.
Separately, the IGC said it planned to meet on Eurotunnel on Wednesday or Thursday.
The Channel Tunnel Safety Authority's report criticised Eurotunnel's safety management procedures but did not go so far as to call for a change in the basic design of the operator's HGV wagons.
Eurotunnel said it accepted most of the authority's 36 recommendations for changes in safety policies.
"The bulk of the recommendations relate to changes which are either already implemented or in hand," Leva said, adding that the report had endorsed some of the company's safety changes.
Eurotunnel's shares firmed 0.5 pence to 70.5 by 1115 GMT in London. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
